# Colony History
[italic]A short history of Hybrisa for new arrivals, as the Herald's archive tells it.[/italic]
## The Claim LV-759 was surveyed for what lies under its rock, and Tartarus Mining staked the first claims. The early camps were prefab sheds around a landing pad, linked by the cave tunnels that still ring the city. The mining outposts north, east and south of the streets are the oldest buildings on the planet, and they look it.
## A Company City The world sits in Three World Empire territory, but the leases went to Weyland-Yutani, and the Company built a city instead of a camp. The Celestia Gateway Space-Port came first, then the DynaGrid Nexus to power it on geothermal heat, gas and fusion. The Westhaven apartment blocks, the Weymart, the Nova Medica Hospital Complex and the Prospera Grand Hotel followed. The welcome sign at the edge of town still carries the Company wings and the full name, [bold]Hybrisa Prospera[/bold]. The dense core around Central Street is what everyone calls the Metropolitan.
## Law and Order Policing is the business of the [bold]Neroid Sector Policing Authority[/bold], working out of the Ironbridge Precinct with its court room and maximum security ward. The old TSEPA lettering is still on the precinct doors. Company guards run their own checkpoints on the streets and at the cave entrances. Residents learn early which badge to show at which gate, and that the two lists do not always agree.
## The Research Complex Behind the electric fences in the caves stands the Weyland-Yutani Advanced Bio-Genomic Research Complex. It has its own hangar, its own armoury and its own security command. The Company says it studies medicine and materials. The Herald has asked for a tour every year and is still waiting.
## The City Now - The Meridian plant builds and sells vehicles for the whole district. - The TMCC Interstellar Freight Hub moves ore and passengers off world around the clock. - The Resource Recovery Facility takes what the city throws away and burns what it cannot sell. - Under the rain and the neon, the Night Gold Casino, the bars and Pizza Galaxy never close.
The Herald here started on a borrowed printer in the freight hub lounges, as a newsletter for the night shift. We still keep night shift hours.
